def test_01_verify_the_screen_when_user_clicks_on_the_create_your_own_shortcut_arrow_button_in_add_new_shortcuts_screen_C46(self):
        """
        Verify the screen.
        TestRails -> https://hp-testrail.external.hp.com/index.php?/cases/view/46
        """
        self.fc.reset_app()
        self.fc.flow_load_home_screen(skip_value_prop=False)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_add_device_btn()
        self.printers.search_printer_by_ip(self.p.ipAddress)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_printer_device_card()
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_shortcuts_tile(raise_e=False)
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_shortcuts_screen_title()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_add_new_shortcut_btn()
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_add_new_shortcut_screen_title()

automation_scripts_rules.rule: Every manual test step must be classified as either: Explicit (requires direct automation script line), Implicit (handled by framework/setup/previous flow), or Supporting (validation/verification purpose). Classification determines mapping approach.

Implicit steps (setup, preconditions, navigation handled elsewhere) must be documented with exact reasoning in parentheses explaining where/how the step is handled. Format: 'Implicit Step – Required for Test Execution (explanation)'.

Each explicit test step must map to exact automation script method calls using dot notation (object.method()). Multiple script lines for a single test step must be separated by newline character (
).
Verification steps must include assert statements before action methods when validation is required. Format: 'assert self.object.verify_method()' followed by action method if applicable.

Automation methods must follow pattern: self.<page_object>.<action>_<element>_<descriptor>(). Actions include: click, verify, enter, select, wait. Page objects must be descriptive (e.g., hpx_shortcuts).

Every test step must be decomposed into granular intermediary steps covering: element location, verification of element state, action execution, wait/transition handling, and implicit verification of outcome.

Intermediary steps must follow strict sequence: 1) Locate element, 2) Verify element visibility/state, 3) Perform action, 4) Wait for result/transition, 5) Implicit verification. This order ensures reliable automation execution.
Setup and precondition steps must be explicitly documented in intermediary steps even if implicit in automation. Include framework initialization, app state, and environmental prerequisites.
Navigation steps must document transition expectations in intermediary steps. Include source screen, target screen, and implicit verification that navigation completed successfully.
Popup interactions require two-phase approach: 1) Verify popup appearance with assert statement, 2) Perform action on popup element. Both must be documented in intermediary steps.
Supporting steps that validate test case purpose must be marked as 'Supporting Step – Purpose of Test Case Validation' and explain implicit verification approach in parentheses.

Every action that triggers navigation, popup, or state change must include explicit wait/synchronization step in intermediary breakdown. Document wait type (transition complete, element visible, etc.).

Implicit verifications must be documented in intermediary steps explaining what is validated and how (e.g., 'successful execution and no assertion failures', 'element state confirms action completed').
Before any action, intermediary steps must include verification that element is in correct state (visible, enabled, clickable). This prevents flaky automation from premature interactions.

If a manual test step contains multiple actions or validations, it must map to multiple script lines (separated by 
) and multiple intermediary step groups. Maintain 1:1 action-to-automation mapping.
Back button or cancel actions that may trigger confirmation dialogs must be followed by popup verification and confirmation action in both script mapping and intermediary steps.
Generic 'Verify the screen' steps must be interpreted as implicit validation through successful flow execution unless specific elements require explicit assertion. Document approach in mapping.
Steps handled by test framework setup (app launch, initial navigation, authentication) must be marked as Implicit with clear boundary documentation of what framework handles vs. test script.
Page object methods must be reusable across test cases. Use consistent naming patterns and parameter approaches. Document method purpose in intermediary steps for future reference.

Final output must contain three arrays: correlation_steps_to_scripts (test step to script mapping), intermediary_steps (granular breakdown), automation_scripts_rules (comprehensive rules). Must be valid minified JSON.
When creating final output, preserve exact original data from inputs without transformation. Maintain original text, formatting within strings, and structural integrity of provided mappings.
Final JSON output must be completely minified: single line, no whitespace between elements, no formatting. Ensures compact transmission and storage while maintaining parseability.
All mappings and rules must support compliance requirements. Document implicit steps, verification approaches, and framework boundaries to enable audit trail and test case traceability.
Rules and patterns established must be applicable to future test cases. Maintain consistency in classification, naming, breakdown approach, and documentation style across all automation efforts.
Explicit steps requiring automation are identified by presence of actual script method calls (self.object.method()). These represent direct test actions not handled by framework or previous flow.

def test_06_verify_the_behavior_when_user_enables_the_print_destination_toggle_bar_in_add_shortcut_screen_C51(self):
        """
        Verify the behavior when user enables the print destination toggle bar.
        TestRails -> https://hp-testrail.external.hp.com/index.php?/cases/view/51
        """
        self.fc.reset_app()
        self.fc.flow_load_home_screen(skip_value_prop=False)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_add_device_btn()
        self.printers.search_printer_by_ip(self.p.ipAddress)
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_printer_device_card()
        self.hpx_printer_details.click_shortcuts_tile(raise_e=False)
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_shortcuts_screen_title()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_add_new_shortcut_btn()
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.verify_add_new_shortcut_screen_title()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_create_your_own_shortcut()
        self.hpx_shortcuts.click_edit_shortcut_print_toggle_btn()
        assert self.hpx_shortcuts.is_continue_btn_enabled(), "Continue button should be enabled after toggling print option"

test_case_details.title: Verify the behavior, when user Enables the 'Print' destination toggle bar in 'Add Shortcut' screen.
test_case_details.custom_preconds:
1.Make sure that the supported printer is added on the root view.
2.Ensure that the user is logged into the account.
test_case_details.custom_steps:
1.Install and Launch the HPX app.
2.Click on the printer icon on the root view screen.
3.Then click on the shortcuts tile on the device details page.
4.Click on the Add new shortcuts in shortcuts screen.
5.Then click on the Create your own shortcut arrow button.
6.Enable the 'Print' destination toggle bar in 'Add Shortcut' screen
7.Verify the screen.
test_case_details.custom_expected:
User should be able to Enable the 'Print' destination toggle bar in 'Add shortcut' screen.
After enabling the 'Print' destination toggle bar, 'continue' button should be enabled.
